title: v3 jitter mitigation and kernel handoff observability
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Background: After onboarding FlashAttention v3 we observed intermittent tail-latency spikes during multi-tenant bursts and occasional decode jitter when the runtime switches kernels mid-request. Existing mitigations (backoff, basic warmup) reduced frequency but not the amplitude of regressions. Problem: lack of fine-grained observability for kernel handoffs and no realtime signal to smooth transitions when v3 selection oscillates across batches. Goal: build lightweight observability and a probabilistic smoothing shim so the runtime can detect risky handoffs early and softly bias scheduling to reduce decode jitter while preserving throughput and cost goals.
success_metrics: 90th and 99th token-latency reduction vs current baseline during bursty traffic (target: >=20% improvement)
Decrease in kernel-selection oscillation events (measured as >2 switches within 500ms for same request) by >=70%
No more than 5% throughput regression in p95 steady-state for common workloads
acceptance_criteria: Instrumentation: per-request kernel decision trace logged toTrace (sampling 1%) with kernel_id, reason, prof_score, memory_headroom
Smoothing shim implemented: probabilistic holdoff window + confidence decay and feature flags to toggle behavior
Dashboard: grafana panel showing kernel handoff rate, avg decision confidence, correlated token-latency distribution
Canary rollout plan documented and automated with rollback trigger if p99 increases by >10%
Unit + integration tests covering handoff path and fallback behavior under memory pressure
work_items: Design telemetry proto for kernel decision trace and event types
Implement lightweight ring buffer attachable to request context to record kernel decisions
Add smoothing shim to kernel-selector: token-count based hysteresis + decayed confidence score
Build queryable index for sampled traces to enable root-cause on incidents
Create Grafana dashboard and SLO alerts tied to handoff rate and p99 token-latency
Run synthetic burst experiments across representative models (70B, 13B, user-short-session, long-context)
comments: 2025-11-04: Kickoff meeting — aligned on instrumentation fields and sampling budget (1% global). Action: Daniel to draft proto, Sofia to spec dashboard metrics.
2025-11-06: Daniel: prototype ring buffer attached to RequestCtx (PR draft: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/1458). Early microbench shows ~0.8us/request added cost at 1% sampling.
2025-11-09: Telemetry team: added indexing hook to trace shipper; traces show frequent v2->v3->v2 oscillation in synthetic long-context workload at batch sizes >32.
2025-11-11: Experiment: enabled simple holdoff (200ms) reduced oscillations but introduced decode pacing artifacts for short requests — reverted for further tuning.

2025-11-14: Implemented probabilistic holdoff: holds with probability proportional to recent confidence delta; initial A/B shows 25% drop in oscillation events and 12% p99 latency improvement on the long-context cluster. Details in internal doc: confluence.redwood.ai/display/RUNTIME/V3+Handoff+Observability.
2025-11-17: PM review (Aisha Patel): recommended adding canary rollback triggers tied to customer-facing SLOs and a smoke test against embeddings-only routes. Added to acceptance criteria.

2025-11-18: QA started integration tests simulating GPU memory pressure and mixed-precision fallbacks. Identified an edge-case where fallback to v2 during tight headroom can leave stale state; created sub-issue ENG-901235 to address state cleanup.
notes: Try to keep sampling budget low to avoid telemetry cost. The smoothing shim must be reversible via runtime flags and heatmaps to observe long-term cost tradeoffs. Coordinate with Dedicated team before enabling on customer-dedicated pools. PM will coordinate canary windows with on-call.
